title: SecOps-NG Supply-Chain Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the supply-chain evidence stream (F-CP-03). One artifact is produced per (workflow_id, execution_id) when a workflow execution that calls external providers closes; it enumerates the dependency surface that execution resolved against, classifies each dependency for sovereignty against the operator's supplier knowledge base, and pins the attestation freshness so the F-PT-03 supplier-attestation primitive set and the downstream KPI / KRI catalog entries (`kri.suppliers_attestation_stale@v1`, plus `kpi.sovereign_provider_share@v1` / `kri.non_sovereign_call_surge@v1` once they land in `content/metrics/`) consume one stable shape. Discharges the operational half of NIS2 Article 21(2)(d) (per-entity supply-chain risk management) and surfaces each entity's dependency surface in the shape Article 22 needs for the Cooperation Group's Union-level coordinated risk assessment of critical supply chains (the Cooperation Group acts in cooperation with the Commission and ENISA — the framework emits the per-entity artifact, not the Member-State aggregation envelope). Public-bar artifact: provider identifiers are opaque operator-side ids, operator-side strings (owner labels, KB refs) MUST stay role-shaped or URN-shaped, and individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<execution_id>|<captured_at>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Two executions of the same workflow at the same instant against the same dependency set collide deliberately; the same execution re-emitted at the same captured_at stays byte-identical.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow identifier — one of the workflow ids declared under `content/playbooks/<workflow-id>/`. The F-CP-03 SKELETON anchor is `vulnerability_triage` (F-WF-01, Shipped); any workflow whose definition declares one or more external-provider calls is in scope.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Re-runs of the same workflow_id produce distinct execution_ids.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this artifact helps satisfy (typically `nis2:art-21-2-d` plus, where applicable, `nis2:art-22` for the Union-level Cooperation-Group overlay). At least one entry — an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-CP-03 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this artifact. At least one — typically `control.supplier_inventory@v1` and `control.provider_attestation@v1`.

dependencies.description: One record per external dependency the execution resolved against. Empty array is invalid — a supply-chain evidence artifact for an execution with zero external dependencies should not be emitted at all (the workflow is not in scope for the stream). The shared emitter (lands in F-CP-03 CORE-FANOUT) enforces this above the schema floor.

aggregates.description: Optional pre-computed counts the emitter may carry so downstream rollups skip re-derivation. Catalog metrics may compute these themselves from `dependencies[]`; the fields reserve the shape for emitters that already track them. All values are non-negative integers.

sovereign_count.description: Count of distinct `provider_id`s whose `sovereignty_classification.sovereignty_band` is `sovereign`. Non-negative integer.

eu_hosted_count.description: Count of distinct `provider_id`s whose `sovereignty_classification.residency` ∈ {eu, eea}. Non-negative integer.

non_eu_count.description: Count of distinct `provider_id`s whose `sovereignty_classification.residency` = `non_eu`. Non-negative integer.

ai_provider_count.description: Count of distinct `provider_id`s whose `kind` = `ai_provider`. Promoted as a first-class aggregate because the NIS2 supply-chain overlay and the EU AI Act both single out the AI-provider surface. Non-negative integer.

owner.description: Dated ownership pointer for the supplier-inventory control attestation. Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline.

role.description: Generic role or working-group identifier (e.g. 'supplier-governance@example.org', 'procurement-lead', 'soc-on-call'). Personal names are not used.

assigned_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the role was assigned ownership of the supplier-inventory attestation chain.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this artifact was captured. Stable input to the artifact_id derivation so re-emissions in the same execution at the same instant stay byte-identical.

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

retention.description: Optional retention pointer the operator declares for this evidentiary record. ISO-8601 duration. The community-default value is an open question to be settled in the EXTEND sibling card, mirroring the equivalent F-CP-02 / F-CP-04 deferrals.

dependency_record.description: One external dependency this execution resolved against.

provider_id.description: Stable operator-side identifier for the provider (e.g. `provider.cve_feed_eu@v1`). The provider catalogue is operator-supplied; the framework ships the schema, not the catalogue. Public-bar text: opaque operator id, no commercial brand names baked into the schema.

kind.description: Which kind of dependency this is. Imports the shared vocabulary from schemas/supply_chain_dependency_kind.json.

version.description: Version pin or commit SHA where applicable. `null` for moving-tag hosted services (most `hosted_api` / `ai_provider` / `managed_runtime` records). String shape is intentionally permissive — semver, commit SHA, calendar version, ISO date.

call_count.description: Integer count of calls this execution issued against the provider. 0 is valid and means 'linked but not called this run' — useful for the SBOM-style enumeration without traffic.

sovereignty_classification.description: Per-record sovereign-provider classification. The classification source-of-truth is an operator-supplied private knowledge base; the framework repository never ingests KB contents (see `content/mappings/nis2/article-21-2-d.yaml`). The contract here is the shape the emitter writes when the KB is consulted.

residency.description: Where the provider runs the workload that produces the data the framework reads. Imports schemas/sovereignty_residency.json.

ownership.description: Beneficial-ownership pointer for the provider (NOT registered-office country). Imports schemas/sovereignty_ownership.json.

sub_processor_chain.description: Array of opaque provider ids of declared sub-processors. Empty array means 'provider declares no sub-processors'. `null` means 'the operator's KB has not captured the chain yet' (distinct from 'no sub-processors').

sovereignty_band.description: Single rolled-up verdict derived deterministically from (residency, ownership, sub_processor_chain). Imports schemas/sovereignty_band.json. The helper that computes it lands on the shared emitter in CORE-FANOUT; drift between successive snapshots feeds the EXTEND-drift sibling.

band_rationale.description: Short free-text explanation pinning the band to the input triple. Read by reviewers; not parsed downstream. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names.

kb_ref.description: Opaque pointer into the operator's private supplier-KB (e.g. `supplier-kb://provider-<id>/2026-Q2`). Framework never resolves this; it only carries the pointer for audit reproducibility.

attestation.description: Per-dependency attestation freshness pointer. Mirrors the cadence vocabulary in schemas/attestation_state.json. `kri.suppliers_attestation_stale@v1` reads `next_due_at` against the artifact-level `captured_at`.

state.description: Current attestation state for the provider. Imports the shared four-state vocabulary from schemas/attestation_state.json.

last_reattested_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent attestation event for this provider.

next_due_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the next attestation falls due. `kri.suppliers_attestation_stale@v1` fires when (artifact captured_at > next_due_at).

attestation_ref.description: Operator-side opaque reference for the attestation record (ticket id, document URN, KB pointer). No commentary, no operator branding.

risk_notes.description: Free-text rationale field. Public-bar text: no individual contact names, provider identity only. No operator branding.
